description: 1.18 allows changing index/quantization/disk configuration post-create through update; vector-space-defining properties (size/distance of an existing named vector) cannot be altered through update [DOC collections]
assertion: after creation, size/distance of an existing (named) vector cannot be changed via PATCH update; index/quantization/disk config can

description: default upsert = insert-or-update by id; update_mode variants exist (1.18): insert_only (existing points are not updated), update_only (missing points are not inserted); update_filter restricts the targets [SPEC]
assertion: upsert default semantics: insert new points and update existing ones by id; update_mode=insert_only skips existing ids; update_mode=update_only skips missing ids

description: delete by filter is allowed and matches all points when the filter is empty/matches everything; deleting non-existent ids is an idempotent success
assertion: delete of non-existent point ids returns success (idempotent); filter-based delete removes every matching point (all points when the filter matches all)

description: operations are executed in order inside one batch request; batchable ops: upsert, update_vectors, delete_vectors, set_payload, overwrite_payload, delete_payload, clear_payload, delete_points [DOC points]
assertion: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result

description: pagination is driven by the response's next_page_offset field; passing it as offset continues the scroll; pagination is exhausted when next_page_offset is null
assertion: scroll returns next_page_offset to continue; null next_page_offset means the scroll is exhausted

description: payload-based order_by REQUIRES a payload index supporting ranges on that field, otherwise the request is rejected [DOC points]
assertion: order_by on a payload field is rejected unless a range-capable payload index exists on that field

description: points OR filter must identify the targets; both absent (null) is an error (spec: either a points list or a filter)
assertion: payload targets: exactly one of points-list or filter must identify targets; both null is rejected

description: overwrite replaces the ENTIRE payload of the targeted points (set semantics: keys missing from the new payload are removed)
assertion: after overwrite the point payload equals the provided payload; previously stored keys absent from the new payload are removed

description: clear removes all payload keys of the targeted points
assertion: after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys

description: delete removes only the listed keys; all other payload keys stay untouched
assertion: only the listed payload keys are removed; unlisted keys persist

description: update affects only the specified named vectors of each point; vectors not listed in the request stay unchanged [DOC points]
assertion: updating vectors of a point changes only the named vectors given; the point's other vectors remain unchanged

description: delete removes the named vectors listed in the vector parameter; the unnamed default vector is deletable too; 200 ok / 404
assertion: delete_vectors removes exactly the named vectors listed (the unnamed default vector included) from the targeted points

description: by-id lookup (query = point id) fetches the stored vector of that point; fetched vectors must match the characteristics of the using vector, otherwise an error is returned [DOC search]
assertion: by-id query uses the referenced point's stored vector; if it does not match the using vector characteristics the request errors

description: the groups query API does not allow offset (pagination); the same restriction applies to the legacy search/recommend groups variants [DOC search]
assertion: groups endpoints reject/omit offset pagination; pagination is not available with groups

description: deleting a non-existent payload index succeeds (idempotent success, 200); deleting an index does not delete the underlying data
assertion: delete of a non-existent payload index is an idempotent success; index deletion leaves point data untouched

description: facet works only on a payload field that has an index supporting MatchValue conditions (e.g. keyword index); without a suitable index the request fails with 400 [DOC payload]
assertion: facet on a field without a suitable (keyword-like) payload index is rejected with 400

description: adds a new named vector space to an existing collection (1.18 feature); name conflicts or invalid params return 400
assertion: a new named vector can be added to an existing collection; conflicting names are rejected

description: removes the named vector space together with its stored data; 404 when the vector name or collection is missing
assertion: deleting a named vector removes the vector space and its data from the collection

description: alias changes are ATOMIC: no collection modifications can happen between the alias operations of one request [SPEC description]
assertion: alias operations in one request are applied atomically - no intermediate state is observable and no collection modification can interleave

description: creating a shard key requires a collection created with sharding_method=custom; existing data is NOT retro-sharded onto the new key
assertion: shard keys can only be created on custom-sharded collections; points written before key creation are not retro-sharded

description: deleting a shard key that still holds data fails; the key must be emptied (points deleted) first
assertion: a shard key holding points cannot be deleted; it must be emptied first

description: removing the last peer or self may break raft consensus; force bypasses the safety check; removing a peer hosting the only replica can cause data loss (by-design destructive)
assertion: peer removal is destructive by design: force=true bypasses safety checks, and removal of a peer holding the only replica can lose data; a 200 does not guarantee consensus survival

description: recover removes the cluster metadata of the current peer and restarts it as a single-node cluster from local data; the operation is irrecoverable for removed peers and is meant for permanently-lost quorum
assertion: cluster recovery resets the peer to a single-node cluster from local data; it is destructive for cluster membership state

description: these operations initiate asynchronous transfers - HTTP 200 means the operation was accepted, not completed; progress is observable through the collection cluster info endpoint
assertion: shard move/replicate operations return 200 on acceptance; completion is asynchronous and observable via cluster info (shard_transfers)

description: recovering from an uploaded snapshot replaces the whole collection data with the archive content
assertion: snapshot upload recovery replaces the entire collection content from the archive

description: recovering a shard from an uploaded snapshot replaces the shard data; priority=replica keeps existing data where it conflicts
assertion: shard snapshot upload replaces shard data; with priority=replica existing data is kept on conflict

description: write=true blocks ALL mutation APIs, returning the configured error_message on any write attempt; designed for maintenance windows; write=false releases the lock
assertion: with write=true every mutation request is refused with the configured error_message until the lock is released (write=false)

description: limits are enforced only while enabled=true; in v1.18 this node-wide config supersedes the deprecated collection-level strict_mode max_resident_memory_percent
assertion: quota limits are enforced only when enabled=true; node-wide quotas supersede the deprecated strict-mode memory percent field
